newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER ON EXPORT RECEIPTS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER ON EXPORT RECEIPTS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar finished firmer against most hard currencies on Thursday on the back of export receipts, mostly from tobacco sales, dealers said.
"Lots of money came into the market today and from the way the Zimbabwe dollar closed I don't think the Reserve Bank intervened today," commented one dealer.

The central bank, fearing the local currency would be less it competitive against others if allowed to appreciate in the face of rising inflation, up at 22.4 percent in the year to April from 19.9 percent, has been regularly coming into the market to mop up all excess money.
At Thursday's close the local unit was quoted at 11.3000/3100 against the U.S. dollar compared to Wednesday's 11.3100/3200 and was also firmer against sterling at 18.4900/5120 from 18.5075/5375.
It was at 6.5690/5775 from 6.5880/5980 versus the mark and at 2.5135/5175 on the rand from 2.5140/5160.
